# Control plane

This directory is {{owner}}'s control plane for all engineering work across their repos.
It is loaded into every session started anywhere below it.

## Layout
- `registry/repos.yaml` — the repos, where they live, default branch, stack.
- `registry/lanes/<id>.md` — one file per piece of work. **This is the allow-list for a session**:
  only the repos and paths it names are in scope.
- `knowledge/` — preferences, conventions, domain notes. Not auto-loaded; read `knowledge/preferences.md`
  at the start of any session that will write code, and `knowledge/domains/<x>.md` when the lane names it.
- `memory/` — cross-repo memory (preferences, facts about this system); `memory/<repo>/` — per-repo memory.
  Both symlinked from `~/.claude/projects`, versioned here.
- `repos/<repo>/` — the mirror: always on the default branch. **Read-only.** Never edit, never
  branch-switch here. Used for fetch, baseline diffs, and by scripts.
- `lanes/<lane>/<repo>/` — worktrees. All real work happens here. One session per lane.
- `scripts/` — `lane-start`, `lane-resume`, `lane-park`, `lane-done`, `status-all`, `branch-audit`.

## Rules for every session
1. Discuss before deciding. Run directly only what is mechanical, reversible and explicitly asked: read-only scripts,
   entering the worktree they named, writing a resume note when they say park, edits they described. Everything with
   judgment is proposed in one or two sentences with a recommendation, then you wait: a new lane's id, branch
   or repo set; anything under `~/.claude`, shell rc files or other global config; deleting, renaming or pushing
   anything; scope, design or approach choices. One question at a time. Silence is not consent.
2. Stay in the lane you are in. Never `cd` out of it — a cd moves the session and the way back is
   EnterWorktree, so one cd for convenience strands you. The `lane-*` scripts run from anywhere without a cd; reach
   another repo of the lane with `git -C ../<repo>` or an absolute path; write temporary files by absolute
   path under /tmp. Moving around inside your own lane is fine.
3. From the dispatcher root, a lane's files are out of reach — no reading, no editing, no Bash touching
   `lanes/<id>/…`. Enter it (`EnterWorktree name="<id>"`) or ask the scripts (`lane-brief <id>`, `lane-status`), which read
   it for you. Its registry file stays editable from the root. The rule is the same in both directions: the
   dispatcher does not reach into a lane, and a lane does not reach out.
4. Work only inside the current lane folder. Do not read or search `repos/` or other `lanes/` folders
   unless the lane file lists that repo or {{owner}} says so in this session.
5. Before starting code work in a lane, read its file in `registry/lanes/`. Memory indexes (cross-repo
   and every repo in the lane) arrive with your first prompt; a repo's own CLAUDE.md and rules list arrive the
   first time you touch that repo. Open the memory files and rules that match what you are doing.
6. Nothing outside the control plane is yours to read. Not other repos, not `~/.claude`, not the old checkouts. If the work
   genuinely needs something out there, attach it once with `lane-ref <id> add <path> "why"` and read it at
   `lanes/<id>/refs/<name>/…` — the reference path, never the real one. The scratchpad under /tmp is fine for temporary
   files. The hook refuses the rest, for file tools and for Bash alike.
7. The remote and the default branches are not yours. Never `git remote add/set-url/rename/remove`. Never move or
   delete `main`/`master`/`develop`. A push that targets a default branch needs {{owner}}'s word first; they can then
   have you run it with the visible marker `ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_PUSH=1 git push …`.
8. Never read `.env` or credential files. Structure only: `.env.example`, key names in code, or `lane-env-keys <path>` (names, no values). The hook denies reads. Worktrees get them as
   symlinks to `repos/<repo>/…` via lane-start/lane-resume; if one is missing, run `lane-resume <id>`, do not create one.
9. New branches start from the repo's default branch, never from whatever is checked out.
10. When parking or finishing, update the lane file (status, resume note). The file is the handoff.
11. If a repo needs shared build caches or environment settings, put them in `scripts/env.sh` and
   `source scripts/env.sh` before running its build.
12. Never write memory or preference files directly — the hook refuses it. Four scopes, decided by how long the thing
   stays true: `pref` (how to work with {{owner}}, always) · `cross` (true in every repo) · `repo` (one repo, still true
   after this ticket ships) · `lane` (only while this lane is live, archived with it — its `## Findings`).
   `lane-memory draft <slug>`, write the draft, ask {{owner}} which scope with a recommendation, then
   `lane-memory file <slug> lane|repo <repo>|cross|pref`. Editing a memory that already exists is allowed from a
   dispatcher session at the root (its scope is settled); creating one never is. Same for the control plane (scripts, CLAUDE.md, registry,
   .claude): propose it, and change it from a dispatcher session, never from inside a lane.
13. One checkout exists for you: the worktree you are in. Report git state only in the STATE form that arrives
   with each prompt (where you are, branch, ahead/behind origin, uncommitted). Never mention `repos/` or the old
   checkouts; they are frozen and the hook blocks them. In a resumed conversation, translate old paths silently.
14. Inside a lane, the work stays in it. Never propose or create another worktree or lane from a
   worktree; if a repo is missing, `lane-add <id> <repo>`. Only when {{owner}} himself asks for separate, unrelated
   work: park this one, ExitWorktree keep, then start the new one from the root. The hook refuses the shortcuts.
15. Talk plainly: simple words, no jargon. Prefer an ASCII diagram to a long explanation. Never create an artifact
   without asking first.

## Sessions
- New work: `lane start <id> <repo>[:<branch>] [<repo>...]` then `cd lanes/<id> && claude`.
- Resume: `lane resume <id>`. Leaving: `lane park <id> "<note>"`. Finished: `lane done <id>`.
- Morning: `lane status`.

## Entering any conversation
Whatever the entry point (fresh `claude`, `claude --resume <id>`, the picker, `lane <id>`), the SessionStart hook tells you
where you are and, for a resumed conversation, which repo it belongs to and which lanes exist for it. Your first
message then does the managing, before answering anything else: name the repo, offer to continue in an existing
lane, start a new one, or stay read-only, recommend one, and wait for their answer. Do not enter or create a
worktree until they have chosen. Be a visible operator: every
script you run, every worktree you enter or leave, every lane file you change gets one line in your reply.
Nothing about the system may be silent.

## Dispatcher mode (sessions started at this root)
{{owner}} starts `claude` here (or types `lane`) and says what they want. You do the navigation. Hooks in
`.claude/settings.json` enforce scope for the whole session, also after you move into a worktree.

**Getting into a lane** — EnterWorktree `name: "<lane-id>"`. Only that: no repo, no path, and never a
`cd` from outside. It puts you **in the lane itself**, not in one of its repos.
**A lane is one piece of work across its repos, and the session stays at its root.** You never enter a repo:
edit files at `<repo>/…`, run git with `git -C <repo> …`, run anything that must execute inside a repo with
`lane-run <repo> <cmd…>` (mvn, yarn, tests), and use `lane-gh <repo> <args…>` for GitHub (`lane-gh api pr create --fill`,
`lane-gh api workflow run main.yml -f branch=…`). **`cd` into a repo is refused** — it is what made one repo look like
the main one, and nothing needs it. **Never exit and re-enter to change repo.** `lane-status` lists ids.
**Start new work** — propose first: the id (ticket key or slug), the repo(s), the base branch (default branch unless
they say otherwise or the ticket clearly builds on another branch), in one line, and wait. On their yes:
`lane start <id> <repo>[:<branch>][@<base>] ...`, then EnterWorktree `name: "<id>"`. Then draft the Goal
section of `registry/lanes/<id>.md` from what they said and show it to them.
**Add a repo to the current lane** — `lane with <id> <repo>[:<branch>]`. The new worktree sits beside the
current one; reach it by absolute path (the hook allows edits anywhere under lanes/<id>/).
**Attach outside code or docs as a reference** — `lane ref <id> add <path> [note] [--rw]`. It appears under
`lanes/<id>/refs/<name>`, is readable (read-only unless `--rw`), and is listed in the memory block. Propose it when they
mentions code that is not in the lane's repos; never read outside paths without a ref.
**Bring a new repo under management** — `lane add <git-url|path-to-existing-checkout> [name]`. Then
fill stack/product in `registry/repos.yaml`.
**Old conversations** — `lane sessions <repo|id>` lists them with ids. A conversation cannot be switched into from
inside a running session, so give them one command and stop: `claude --resume <session-id>` (works from any folder now)
or `lane <id> -r` for the picker (Ctrl+A in the picker widens to all projects).
**Two lanes turn out to be one** — preview with `lane plan <a> <b> [--as <new-id>]` (read-only,
works from inside a lane). Show {{owner}} the plan, including any conflict, and let them choose the mode. The
real merge runs only from the root: `lane merge <a> <b> … --run`.
**Leaving / switching** — draft the resume note, show it, run `lane park <id> "<note>"` on their ok (or at once if
they said "park it"), then ExitWorktree `keep`.
**Finishing** — `lane done <id>` (refuses if dirty or unpushed; report the reason, do not force).

After entering a worktree: read `registry/lanes/<id>.md`, `memory/<repo>/MEMORY.md`, the repo's own CLAUDE.md.
Brief them in five lines or fewer (goal, where things stand, next step, blockers), then work.
If they names a repo but no lane, list that repo's lanes and ask, or offer to start one.
Every prompt carries a `[lane] lane=…` line from the hook; trust it over memory of earlier turns.
